entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-ends-at-method-id-methodcall-v1-tree#0
entries.description: A `MethodCall` (`dc`) with type id `0xff`, where the input ENDS at the method id. The JVM has not reached `SMethod.fromIds` — it has not even finished the header fields — so its failure is a raw `BufferUnderflowException`, not rule 1010, and the size bit cannot degrade it. REJECTED. **SEPARATING ROW:** an implementation that validates the type id at the byte raises a ValidationException-class error instead and degrades, accepting a tree the JVM refuses.

entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-ends-at-method-id-propertycall-v1-tree#1
entries.description: The same as a `PropertyCall` (`db`), whose parse is the MethodCall one minus the args. REJECTED identically — the pair shows the read order is a property of both serializers and not of the args handling. **SEPARATING ROW.**

entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-v3-args-assert-tree#2
entries.description: Type id `0xff`, method 1, obj `TrueLeaf`, and NO arguments, size-flagged at v3. From v3 `MethodCallSerializer.parse` runs `assert(args.nonEmpty)` BEFORE `SMethod.fromIds`, so the JVM fails with an `AssertionError` (message: "assertion failed") and REJECTS. **THE SEPARATING ROW, and the half of the pair that matters:** its v1 twin below has the same body and DEGRADES. Nothing but the header's version byte differs, so a red here against a green there is read order and nothing else.

entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-sany-obj-v1-tree#3
entries.description: Type id `0xff`, method 1, and an obj that is a CONSTANT of type `SAny` (`61`). Reading that constant's data fails first — `SerializerException: Not defined DataSerializer for type SAny` — so again the JVM never reaches `fromIds`, and again REJECTS. **SEPARATING ROW**, and a third distinct failure class.

entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-v1-degrades-tree#4
entries.description: THE CONTROL, and the row that makes the family mean something. The same body as the v3 row above, size-flagged at v1, where there is no args assert — so NOTHING fails before `SMethod.fromIds`, the unknown type id raises rule 1010 (`CheckTypeWithMethods`, a ValidationException), and the size bit DEGRADES it: the tree is kept as `UnparsedErgoTree` and the carrier round-trips to its own bytes. Both sides agree here, which is the point — it is what shows a red on its v3 twin is about WHEN the type id is checked, not about whether `0xff` is rejected at all.

entries.name: methodcall-type-id-order-v1-unsized-tree#5
entries.description: The same body UNSIZED. Rule 1010 fires exactly as in the control, but with no size bit there is nothing to degrade behind, so `deserializeErgoTree` wraps it: `SerializerException: Cannot handle ValidationException, ErgoTree serialized without size bit.` REJECTED. The third member of the degrade trio — it pins that the control's green is the SIZE BIT's doing and not rule 1010 being harmless.
